title: 12-Lead ECG
author: T. Eskridge, MD
summary: Sinus tachycardia 118 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 432 ms (Bazett). Normal upright T waves, no U waves, no ST depression; rate-related tachycardia from dehydration and ketoacidosis.
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 118 bpm. PR 142 ms. QRS 82 ms. QTc 432 ms (Bazett). Axis +40 degrees (mild leftward shift is normal at 28 weeks).

**Interpretation**
Regular sinus tachycardia, no ectopy. Normal upright T waves in all leads, no U waves, no ST depression or elevation.

**Context**
Recorded during ketoacidosis with 36 hours of vomiting at 28 weeks 2 days; potassium result pending. Tachycardia is expected from volume depletion and acidosis (and is partly physiologic in pregnancy).
impression: Sinus tachycardia 118 bpm. Normal T waves, no U waves. QTc 432 ms.

title: 12-Lead ECG
author: T. Eskridge, MD
summary: Sinus rhythm 98 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 478 ms (Bazett; T-U fusion). Diffusely flattened T waves (I, II, aVL, V3-V6), 0.5 mm ST depression V4-V6 and prominent U waves (1.5 mm V2-V4). Hypokalemia pattern (potassium 3.2, magnesium 1.5); no ectopy.
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 98 bpm. PR 164 ms. QRS 88 ms. QTc 478 ms (Bazett; the T and U waves are fused, so this is a QTc/QUc). Axis +35 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Sinus rhythm, no premature beats. Diffusely **flattened T waves** (I, II, aVL, V3-V6), **prominent upright U waves** (1.5 mm in V2-V4, taller than the T wave) and **0.5 mm horizontal ST depression in V4-V6**. Compared with 0145: rate slower (118 to 98), new T flattening, U waves and ST depression.

**Context**
Recorded at 0710 after the critical potassium of 3.2 mEq/L with magnesium 1.5 mg/dL (insulin infusion running since 0215). The pattern fits insulin-driven hypokalemia with low magnesium. QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron) should be avoided until potassium and magnesium are corrected. Repeat when the potassium has been replaced.
impression: Sinus rhythm 98 with flat T waves, prominent U waves and 0.5 mm ST depression V4-V6 at potassium 3.2. QTc 478 ms (T-U fusion).

title: 12-Lead ECG
author: T. Eskridge, MD
summary: Sinus rhythm 90 bpm, PR 156 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 452 ms (Bazett). T waves improving (low but upright in V3-V6), ST segments isoelectric, U waves smaller (0.5 mm). Potassium 3.6 after 20 mEq replacement.
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 90 bpm. PR 156 ms. QRS 86 ms. QTc 452 ms (Bazett). Axis +35 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Sinus rhythm. T waves have recovered to low upright waves in V3-V6, ST segments are isoelectric and the U waves are much smaller (0.5 mm). No ectopy. Compared with 0710: ST depression gone, QTc 478 to 452 ms.

**Context**
Recorded at the insulin restart (potassium 3.6 after two riders of 10 mEq and magnesium 2 g running). Continue potassium replacement to a goal of 4.0 or higher while the insulin runs.
impression: Sinus rhythm 90. T waves recovering, small U waves, no ST depression at potassium 3.6. QTc 452 ms.

title: 12-Lead ECG
author: T. Eskridge, MD
summary: Normal sinus rhythm 84 bpm, PR 148 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 424 ms (Bazett). Normal upright T waves in all leads, no U waves, normal ST segments. Hypokalemic changes resolved (potassium 4.1).
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 84 bpm. PR 148 ms. QRS 82 ms. QTc 424 ms (Bazett). Axis +35 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Normal sinus rhythm. Crisp normal upright T waves in all leads, no U waves, normal ST segments. Complete resolution of the hypokalemic repolarization changes seen at 0710 and 0935.

**Context**
Recorded after the 1850 panel (potassium 4.1, magnesium 2.0, DKA resolved). Telemetry can continue as ordered.
impression: Normal sinus rhythm 84. T waves normal, no U waves. QTc 424 ms.
